channel.description: New research across consciousness, quantum foundations, and neuroscience.

item.title: Qutrit quantum neural network with non-commutative multi-subspace feature map
item.description: We present QNN-3L, a quantum neural network architecture based on three-level systems (qutrits) with longitudinal Ising-type couplings on a one-dimensional lattice. Starting from an explicit phenomenological multilevel Hamiltonian that includes local anharmonicity, diagonal couplings and resonant control pulses, we derive native selective rotations on computational subspaces and a nearest-neighbour controlled-\((Z)\) primitive.

item.title: Benchmarking and resource analysis for augmented-Lagrangian quantum Hamiltonian descent
item.description: Quantum Hamiltonian Descent (QHD) is a continuous optimization algorithm based on simulating a time-dependent quantum Hamiltonian whose potential energy encodes the objective function and whose kinetic energy promotes exploration through quantum interference and tunneling. While QHD is formulated for unconstrained optimization, many real-world optimization problems are constrained and highly nonconvex.

item.title: Large-Scale Streaming Portfolio Optimization with Pauli Correlation Encoding
item.description: Classical portfolio construction over large asset universes is a combinatorial selection problem that existing heuristics do not solve well at scale. Pauli Correlation Encoding (PCE) addresses this by representing the underlying clustering problem with far fewer qubits than one per asset, and a prior study showed it is competitive with classical methods on a single historical snapshot.

item.title: Tunable spectral correlations of highly multimode visible light via broadband quantum frequency conversion
item.description: Multimode squeezed states of light are a resource for achieving quantum advantage in computing and sensing, where spatial or temporal modes have been the experimental norm. In our experiments, we generated highly frequency-multimode infrared quantum light and showed how adiabatic frequency conversion can be used to convert the quantum state to visible wavelengths while concurrently manipulating the joint spectrum by realizing a configurable many-port frequency-domain beamsplitter unitary transformation.

item.title: Time Travel Paradoxes and Entangled Timelines
item.description: For time travel to be consistent with the known laws of physics, the resulting paradoxes must be resolved. It has been suggested that the notion of parallel timelines may provide a resolution, by allowing different events to happen in different timelines.

item.title: Decoding sequence auditory expectations for clinical diagnostic and prognostic assessment of prolonged disorders of consciousness
item.description: Objective.Electroencephalogram (EEG) features are important objective markers for diagnostic and prognostic evaluation of prolonged disorders of consciousness (DOC). item.title: Dopamine dynamics in a mouse model of temporal lobe seizures with impaired consciousness
item.description: OBJECTIVE: Focal temporal lobe seizures often lead to impaired consciousness. Recent work has shown depressed cortical arousal, with slow waves and decreased cortical acetylcholine as a possible mechanism for impaired consciousness in focal seizures.

item.title: Does the Workspace Do the Work? A Causal Protocol for Verifying Global-Workspace Computation in a Language Model
item.description: Global Workspace Theory (GWT), a leading theory of consciousness, holds that information becomes conscious when it is broadcast to specialized processes that use it. Building a workspace into a network does not reveal what the trained network computes with it: a module that reports an answer may have combined a broadcast message with its own knowledge, or merely forwarded an answer computed elsewhere, and task accuracy and ablation cannot tell these apart.

item.title: Resource-Efficient Quantum Classifier for Facial Identification
item.description: Hybrid quantum frameworks are typically associated with higher-dimensional and complex problems. Their applicability to resource-constrained biometric systems remain insufficiently explored.

item.title: Theory-Informed Quantum Error Mitigation for Shor Order Finding with Fourier Neural Operators
item.description: Quantum noise distorts the distribution of circuit measurement outcomes, often leaving enough information to infer the algorithm's correct result. To recover this latent information from the noisy distribution in Shor order finding, we introduce a theory-informed quantum error mitigation method.

item.title: Quantum Community Detection for Data Analysis
item.description: Community detection offers an alternative to conventional methods for data analysis tasks such as feature selection and clustering, and detecting communities with quantum algorithms is a promising avenue for quantum speedup. We investigate quantum spectral community detectors, such as the modularity-matrix algorithm deteQt, in pipelines for both tasks.

item.title: Witnessing Gaussian Coexistence and Correlation-Ellipse Tomography
item.description: Gaussian light is specified by second-order field moments, yet their hidden correlation geometry can demand higher-order intensity measurements. We establish a measurement hierarchy for "Gaussian coexistence", i.e., the simultaneous presence of cross covariance and cross pseudocovariance.

item.title: Quantum optimization beyond qubit count by low-energy subspace sampling
item.description: On current digital quantum devices, standard one-qubit-per-variable encodings restrict quantum optimization algorithms to problem sizes where classical solvers typically excel. To avoid this constraint, we introduce Quantum Subspace Sampling Descent (QSSD), an iterative heuristic that decouples the number of problem variables from qubit count, while preserving knowledge of the problem's global structure.

item.title: Quantum Tautochrone for photons and atoms
item.description: The tautochrone problem, in which the travel time to a common point is independent of the starting position, has served as a foundational model in classical mechanics. Here we establish its quantum counterpart in engineered photonic waveguide arrays and atomic optical lattices, where nonuniform couplings drive photons and particles launched from different positions to converge simultaneously at a common site.
